criteria.criterion: xtask/src/shard.rs lets a unit carry a test-name filter (module prefixes plus a skip-based catch-all), prints it in the --dry-run line, and runs it as `cargo test --locked -p athena-core --lib -- <filter>`; Grep of xtask/shard-timings.txt shows athena-core --lib as at least two part lines, not one.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff. `Unit` gains `filter: Option<Filter>` (`only` plus `skip`). `Unit::line()` appends ` -- <args>`. `cargo_args()` builds `-p athena-core --lib -- <args>`, and both `command` and `timings_command` run it after `test --locked`. `core_lib_filters()` adds the catch-all that skips every listed prefix. Lines 51-56 of xtask/shard-timings.txt hold six `athena-core --lib -- ...` part lines and no whole `athena-core --lib` line.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo run -p xtask -- test-shard K 6 --dry-run` for K=0..5: athena-core --lib parts appear in at least two different shards, no part appears twice, and every other target appears exactly once across the shards.
criteria.evidence: Where the six parts landed: shard 1 has hestia/run, shard 2 admission/gh/land, shard 3 the catch-all, shard 4 evidence_labels/reading, and shard 5 checks/... and disk/.... Shard 0 has none. No part line repeats. I read all six outputs, and each other target appears once. The ci_shards test test_shard_6_is_disjoint_and_equals_the_workspace_target_set also passed.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p xtask --test shard_parts` and `cargo test -p xtask --test ci_shards`: a test checks every name from `cargo test -p athena-core --lib -- --list` matches exactly one part's filter, and a negative test shows a dropped or duplicated prefix is rejected.
criteria.evidence: shard_parts: 5 passed. These include every_athena_core_lib_test_is_kept_by_exactly_one_part, which takes names from `cargo test --locked -p athena-core --lib -- --list --format terse` and parts from the dry-run output and checks more than 700 names, plus a_dropped_prefix_is_rejected and a_duplicated_prefix_is_rejected. ci_shards: 21 passed, including the new cover_rejects_a_target_run_whole_and_as_parts.

findings.summary: Clippy fails on the new test file, so the 'tested' default (clippy clean) is broken.
findings.evidence: Athena's record: `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` failed (CI run 41560938422). I reproduced it with `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`: "error: called `filter(..).next()` on an `Iterator`. This is more succinctly expressed by calling `.find(..)`" (clippy::filter_next). The fix is `.iter_mut().find(|p| ...)`.

findings.summary: The prefixes are matched as substrings, so short ones like `run::`, `state::`, `plan::` and `status::` would also match any nested module with the same name.
findings.evidence: libtest's positional filter and `--skip` match substrings, so a future `gh::tests::run::x` would be kept by two parts. The coverage test in shard_parts.rs would catch that (it passes today), so this is a maintenance hazard, not a bug. The test-name filter could not anchor at the start of the name anyway, so the coverage test is the right safety net.

findings.summary: The timings comment says 823 tests in the source but everything else says 821.
findings.evidence: Line 9 reads "counted from #[test] attributes, 823 in the source", while shard.rs doc comments and CHANGELOG say 821 (the run's count). It is a small inconsistency for an outside reader.

findings.summary: shard_parts.rs runs nested `cargo test --list` and the six dry-runs once per test, about 51s in total.
findings.evidence: lib_test_names() and parts_from_dry_run() are called separately in three or four tests. The measured run took 50.93s. They could be computed once, for example with a OnceLock.

summary: The change does what was asked. `xtask test-shard` now splits `athena-core --lib` into six parts by test-name prefix, one of which is a `--skip` catch-all for every other test. The dry-run lists for K=0..5 put those parts on shards 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5, with no part listed twice. The new coverage test lists every library test and checks that each one matches exactly one part, and it rejects a dropped or duplicated prefix. All targeted tests pass. The timings file and CHANGELOG carry the requested numbers, and my estimated shard totals are balanced (about 194–197s each). The verdict is still fail: Athena's recorded `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` failed, and I reproduced it. `xtask/tests/shard_parts.rs:139` uses `.filter(..).next()`, which trips clippy::filter_next. That breaks the "tested" default (clippy clean). Changing it to `.find(..)` fixes it.
